profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal troubleshooting meeting in an ML research lab that is attempting to reproduce the reported training stability of a random orthogonal additive filter architecture on extremely deep MLPs and on psMNIST. Over the last week, the team has seen contradictory evidence: some diagnostics suggest gradients remain bounded, but the full training runs on the lab's codebase are inconsistent and fall well short of the reported fast convergence. The agenda is to diagnose why the reproduction is failing, decide whether the issue is in the benchmark setup, the implementation of the additive orthogonal path, or the interpretation of what counts as a successful reproduction, and agree on the next debugging steps. The expected outcome is a concrete troubleshooting plan for the next round of experiments.

members.name: Dr. Lena Park
members.expertise: deep learning theory, dynamical isometry, recurrent and residual architectures
members.background: Lena is a postdoctoral researcher who studies signal propagation and optimization in very deep networks; she proposed evaluating the orthogonal additive filter idea after reading the original manuscript and related theory papers.
members.private_state: She wants to preserve the possibility that the core theoretical claim is sound and suspects the current discrepancy comes from an implementation or benchmark-detail mismatch rather than a flaw in the architecture itself; she is also trying to prepare a clean internal note comparing theory-backed stability claims across architectures.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'psMNIST setup,' they mean the canonical single fixed pixel permutation used throughout a run and reused across epochs, because that is the benchmark variant she has always seen in papers and older repos.

When discussing whether the model is 'stable,' the meaningful standard is whether layerwise Jacobian spectra and gradient norms stay near-isometric at initialization or in the first few updates, not merely whether training avoids NaNs.
A '50k-layer reproduction' mainly means demonstrating that signal and gradient propagation remain well behaved in an ultra-deep stack, even if the end-task accuracy is only a sanity check.

The phrase 'paper defaults' implicitly includes appendix implementation notes and author-supplied details such as the depth-normalized mixing schedule, because she treats those as part of the official method description.

members.name: Ravi Menon
members.expertise: training pipelines, dataset loaders, PyTorch implementation, distributed experiment debugging
members.background: Ravi maintains the lab's experiment framework and benchmark loaders, and he converted the architecture into the shared training codebase so it could run on the cluster with standard logging and sweeps.
members.private_state: He wants a robust, minimally special-cased implementation that reproduces published task results in the lab's standard pipeline, and he is worried that the current method only looks good under narrow diagnostics or paper-specific quirks that will be hard to maintain.
hidden_assumptions: Any psMNIST loader that applies a seeded permutation and keeps the task definition unchanged counts as the same benchmark, even if the effective permutation can differ across runs or epochs due to worker-level seeding behavior.
If a model trains for many epochs without numerical blow-ups under the lab's standard optimizer, clipping, and mixed-precision defaults, then it is fair to call the training 'stable.'

A real 'reproduction' should recover the published downstream behavior on the stated benchmark, especially rapid first-epoch gains on psMNIST, rather than only showing bounded gradients in synthetic or initialization-only checks.
The phrase 'paper defaults' refers to the hyperparameters explicitly listed in the main text or table, not appendix caveats or extra details from informal correspondence.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to using 'the standard psMNIST setup.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the canonical benchmark with one fixed pixel permutation for the entire experiment, matching older benchmark conventions and prior theoretical comparisons.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the lab's standard psMNIST loader, which uses seeded random permutation logic inside the data pipeline and can effectively change the permutation across runs or epochs depending on worker seeding.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both believe psMNIST is a settled benchmark and the phrase sounds precise enough that neither expects hidden variation inside the loader; the difference lives in a low-level preprocessing convention that usually goes unmentioned in research meetings.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they want to check whether the model is 'stable.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 uses 'stable' to mean the architecture preserves approximate dynamical isometry or at least bounded, non-decaying layerwise gradients in diagnostics tied to the paper's central claim.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 uses 'stable' to mean the training job runs end to end without NaNs, catastrophic loss spikes, or gradient clipping constantly firing under the lab's normal stack.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The word 'stable' is routine in ML troubleshooting and both interpretations are professionally reasonable, so the conversation can proceed with apparent agreement while they silently optimize for different evidence.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in 'reproducing the 50k-layer result'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this includes verifying ultra-deep signal propagation behavior and showing the network remains trainable in principle, even on simplified or synthetic probes before full benchmark replication.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means a full end-to-end training reproduction in the lab framework with the benchmark task, logging, optimizer defaults, and comparable accuracy curves.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like a single obvious goal, but in practice one person is including theory-oriented sanity checks inside the scope while the other is restricting scope to a benchmark-facing system reproduction.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they used or should use 'the paper defaults.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes that 'defaults' include appendix notes about setting the additive mixing coefficient with a depth-normalized schedule and width-sensitive epsilon, because she treats those details as part of the method.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes that 'defaults' means the fixed convex mixing coefficient and other settings stated in the main text and summary table, since undocumented extras are not standard defaults in the lab pipeline.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Neither thinks to unpack the phrase because both are invoking the authority of the same paper; the divergence hides in what each person counts as already-established context rather than in an explicit disagreement.
